headline: Research firm IDC says about 25,000 humanoid robots were shipped worldwide in the first half of 2026, with China's AgiBot shipping the most.
score_reason: Kept at 6: specific, internally consistent IDC figures, but they reach us second-hand through one outlet that also repeats AgiBot's deployments without attribution.
importance_line: It shows humanoid robots moving from demonstrations to thousands of shipped units, mostly in China, but the figures are one research firm's estimates and say nothing about how much useful work the robots do.
summary: Gasgoo reports, citing research firm IDC, that global humanoid robot shipments neared 25,000 units in the first half of 2026, up 432.1% on a year earlier, with China taking about 77.9% and AgiBot of China shipping more than 8,600 units, about 35% of the world total. IDC projects shipments will exceed 750,000 units by 2030, which is a forecast, and the article's examples of AgiBot robots at work, including more than 300 at a tourist park in Hengqin, are given without independent confirmation.
notes: IDC's release itself was not seen; the release date is not stated in the article.
